cross_references.label: CMIA — Authorized Disclosures
cross_references.note: §56.35 damages attach to violations of §56.10. A disclosure that falls outside the enumerated exceptions in §56.10(b) and (c) is the predicate act that triggers §56.35 liability.

cross_references.label: CMIA — Criminal Penalties and Enhanced Civil Liability
cross_references.note: §56.36 provides criminal penalties (misdemeanor/felony) and enhanced civil liability for individuals who intentionally obtain medical information for personal gain or to harm a patient. §56.35 governs standard civil damages; §56.36 applies when the misconduct rises to criminal-level intent.

cross_references.label: Tort Damages — Consequential and Emotional Distress
cross_references.note: §56.35(c) incorporates §3333 as the measure of actual damages for intentional/knowing CMIA violations. §3333 includes consequential damages, emotional distress damages, and economic losses.

cross_references.label: Medical Malpractice SOL — Health Care Provider Defendants
cross_references.note: When a CMIA defendant is a health care provider, the one-year medical malpractice SOL under CCP §340.5 may apply. For non-provider defendants, the general two-year personal injury SOL under CCP §335.1 applies.

cross_references.label: General Personal Injury SOL
cross_references.note: Two-year limitations period applies to CMIA claims against non-provider defendants (e.g., employers, insurers, contractors who are not health care providers). Discovery rule tolls the period when the violation was concealed.

cross_references.label: CMIA Definitions
cross_references.note: §56.05 defines 'provider of health care,' 'health care service plan,' 'contractor,' and other terms that determine who is subject to §56.35 liability.

cross_references.label: Federal PHI Use and Disclosure Rules
cross_references.note: HIPAA §164.502 establishes the federal floor for PHI use and disclosure. CMIA is stricter than HIPAA in many respects; the California standard governs California-based providers. Both may be violated simultaneously by an unauthorized disclosure.
